pr_title: systemd-sleep: replace rtc wakealarm with CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM s2h
pr_body: Completes `sleep.c` task in [TODO](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/TODO#L32) to replace rtc ioctls with `CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM` and fixes issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/12567 by removing `/sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm` dependency.
pr_comments: I think this is ready for review. Any feedback or suggestions would be helpful. This solves an issue I'm occasionally experiencing on my laptop so excited to get it fixed. In the meantime, I've posted this [crude work around](https://github.com/zachsmith/x1yg3-suspend-to-ram/blob/master/README.md#sysclassrtcrtc0wakealarm-device-or-resource-busy).

Thanks for the review and the helpful comments, @poettering! I really appreciate you taking the time to provide suggestions. I think I've addressed all of your feedback and was able to cleanup the code a bit more but please let me know if I missed something - especially if I implemented the `poll()` suggestion incorrectly. This is all quite new to me so your comments were very helpful and much appreciated.
Thanks agian, @poettering! I made the changes based on your most recent feedback.
Thanks! Love it! This looks sooo much better than the old /dev/rtc code. Thanks for working on this!
Thanks again, @poettering for all the help getting my first `systemd` PR in good shape!

issue_context.title: logind: suspend-then-hibernate fails completely if /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm has value
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> 241  _systemd 241 (v241-8.git9ef65cb.fc30)_
<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Fedora 30

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > If `/sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm` has a value prior to `suspend-then-hibernate`, it should log a message to the journal indicating that hibernate could not be scheduled and attempt to fall back to suspend only.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > When a `wakealarm` exists prior to `suspend-then-hibernate`, an attempted write to `/sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm` results in an error that prevents the system from entering any suspended state. 

> This is especially important in `LidSwitch` events when the user will likely close the laptop and place in a bag where it can get hot, drain the battery, and potentially cause damage.

**Steps to reproduce**
 
On a system that supports `hibernate`, run the following:

```shell
echo +60 > /sys/class/rtc/rtc0/wakealarm
systemctl suspend-then-hibernate
```
You will observe the system attempt to enter suspend but then wake abruptly. Check the journal for errors.

```shell
journal -b --grep wakealarm
```

review_comments: ts.it_value is not initialized when this is called. please do. for example, by doing `struct itimerspec its = {}` when you declare the structure first.
